source: Clues adapted from Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) and Wikidata (CC0)

clues.q: This 1937 children's fantasy novel by J. R. R. Tolkien was subtitled There and Back Again.
In J. K. Rowling's debut novel, a young wizard receives a letter of acceptance from Hogwarts on his eleventh birthday.
clues.a: What is Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (Sorcerer's Stone)?

clues.q: In this 1865 Lewis Carroll novel, a little girl falls through a rabbit hole into a fantasy world.
clues.a: What is Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?

clues.q: Set in Middle-earth, this high fantasy epic by J. R. R. Tolkien began as a sequel to his 1937 children's book.
clues.a: What is The Lord of the Rings?

clues.q: In this E. B. White book, a barn spider writes messages like "Some Pig" and "Terrific" to save a pig named Wilbur.
In this 1900 L. Frank Baum novel, a Kansas farm girl and her dog Toto are swept away by a cyclone to a magical land.
clues.a: What is The Wonderful Wizard of Oz?

clues.q: In this 1843 Dickens novella, the miser Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by the ghost of Jacob Marley and three spirits.
Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 adventure novel tells a story of "buccaneers and buried gold"; its working title was The Sea Cook.
This 1950 C. S. Lewis fantasy was the first published of the seven novels in The Chronicles of Narnia.
clues.a: What is The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe?

clues.q: In this 1964 Roald Dahl novel, a boy surnamed Bucket gets to go inside the works of an eccentric chocolatier named Willy Wonka.
clues.a: What is Charlie and the Chocolate Factory?

clues.q: This 1876 Mark Twain novel about a boy growing up along the Mississippi River is set in the fictional town of St. Petersburg.
clues.a: What is The Adventures of Tom Sawyer?

clues.q: In this 1837 Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, a young sea princess is willing to give up her life in the sea to gain a human soul.
This Grimm fairy tale features a magic mirror, a poisoned apple, a glass coffin, an Evil Queen and seven dwarfs.
In this Grimm fairy tale, two abandoned siblings find a witch's house made of bread, cake and sugar, and the sister pushes the witch into her own oven.
In this 1812 Brothers Grimm fairy tale, an imp spins straw into gold in exchange for a woman's firstborn child.
In this fable, a Big Bad Wolf blows down houses of straw and sticks but cannot destroy one made of bricks.
clues.a: What is The Three Little Pigs?

clues.q: This 1894 Rudyard Kipling story collection features Shere Khan the tiger, Baloo the bear, and Mowgli, a "man-cub" raised by wolves.
This 1719 Daniel Defoe adventure novel about a castaway has been described as the first novel in English.
In this 2008 Suzanne Collins novel, Katniss Everdeen of Panem takes her sister Primrose's place in a deadly annual event.
Carlo Collodi's 1883 Italian novel follows a mischievous marionette whose heart's desire is to become a real boy.
clues.a: What is The Adventures of Pinocchio?

clues.q: This Homeric epic follows the king of Ithaca on his ten-year journey home after the Trojan War.
Often called the first substantial piece of European literature, this Greek epic poem attributed to Homer has 24 books and 15,693 lines.
George Orwell's final completed book, published in 1949, centres on totalitarianism and mass surveillance.
In this 1945 Orwell novella, mistreated animals rebel against their human master, only to end up under the dictatorship of the pigs.
This 1813 Jane Austen novel of manners follows Elizabeth Bennet, who learns the repercussions of hasty judgments.
Subtitled The Modern Prometheus, this 1818 Gothic novel was begun by its author when she was just 18.
Bram Stoker's 1897 Gothic horror novel opens with Jonathan Harker visiting the castle of a Transylvanian nobleman.
In this 1851 Herman Melville novel, narrated by Ishmael, Captain Ahab of the Pequod seeks revenge on a giant white whale.
Harper Lee's 1960 Southern Gothic novel won the Pulitzer Prize and is widely read in American middle and high schools.
clues.a: What is To Kill a Mockingbird?

clues.q: Written and illustrated by a French aviator and published in 1943, this novella follows a young royal who visits various planets, including Earth.
Jonathan Swift's 1726 satirical prose novel popularised the fictional island of Lilliput.
In this 1872 Jules Verne novel, Phileas Fogg and his valet Passepartout race the clock on a wager of 20,000 pounds.
clues.a: What is Around the World in Eighty Days?

clues.q: Serialised from 1869 to 1870, this Jules Verne science fiction adventure is set aboard Captain Nemo's submarine, the Nautilus.
clues.a: What is Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas?

clues.q: Louisa May Alcott's 1868 coming-of-age novel follows the four March sisters: Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy.
In Charles Dickens's second novel, an orphan escapes a workhouse to London and meets a gang of pickpockets led by Fagin.
This book collects the writings of a Jewish teenager who hid with her family for two years during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands.
clues.a: What is The Diary of a Young Girl (The Diary of Anne Frank)?

clues.q: In this 1908 Canadian novel by Lucy Maud Montgomery, siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert get an 11-year-old orphan girl by mistake instead of a boy.
clues.a: What is Anne of Green Gables?

clues.q: This 1880s Johanna Spyri novel follows a five-year-old girl in her grandfather's care in the Swiss Alps.
This 1871 Lewis Carroll sequel sends its young heroine on a new adventure whose theme is chess.
Jack London's 1903 novel follows Buck, a dog stolen from California and sold as a sled dog during the Klondike Gold Rush.
clues.a: What is The Call of the Wild?

clues.q: Published in two parts in 1605 and 1615, this Cervantes novel about a hidalgo from La Mancha is called the first modern novel.
In this 1925 F. Scott Fitzgerald novel set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, narrator Nick Carraway meets a mysterious millionaire.
This 1884 Mark Twain novel, a direct sequel to the story of Tom Sawyer, is often named among the Great American Novels.
clues.a: What is Adventures of Huckleberry Finn?

clues.q: This 1844 Alexandre Dumas swashbuckler, set between 1625 and 1628, is the first of his d'Artagnan Romances.
In this Alexandre Dumas adventure novel, the young sailor Edmond Dantes is falsely accused of treason and imprisoned in the Chateau d'If.
clues.a: What is The Count of Monte Cristo?

clues.q: This 1862 French epic historical novel by Victor Hugo has been adapted many times, including as a stage musical.
Set during the Napoleonic Wars, this epic novel by Leo Tolstoy mixes a fictional story with chapters on history and philosophy.
Published in 1847 under the pen name "Currer Bell", this Charlotte Bronte bildungsroman follows its heroine's love for the brooding Mr Rochester.
Emily Bronte's only novel concerns the Earnshaw and Linton families on the Yorkshire moors and the foster son Heathcliff.
Dickens's thirteenth novel is a bildungsroman narrated by an orphan nicknamed Pip.
In this 1886 Robert Louis Stevenson novella, the lawyer Utterson investigates a respected doctor's link to a murderous criminal.
clues.a: What is (Strange Case of) Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde?

clues.q: Set on Dartmoor, this third Sherlock Holmes novel has Holmes and Watson investigating the legend of a fearsome supernatural dog.
clues.a: What is The Hound of the Baskervilles?

clues.q: William Golding's 1954 debut novel follows a group of British boys stranded on an uninhabited island who descend into savagery.
clues.a: What is Lord of the Flies?

clues.q: Originally intended for adults, this 1951 J. D. Salinger coming-of-age novel is often read by teens for its themes of angst and alienation.
clues.a: What is The Catcher in the Rye?

clues.q: In this 1953 Ray Bradbury novel, books are outlawed and "firemen" like Guy Montag burn any that are found.
Aldous Huxley's 1932 dystopian novel is set largely in a futuristic global state whose citizens are engineered into a social hierarchy.
Ernest Hemingway's 1952 novella tells of Santiago, an aging fisherman, and his long struggle to catch a giant marlin.
clues.a: What is The Old Man and the Sea?

clues.q: John Steinbeck's 1937 novella follows George Milton and Lennie Small, migrant ranch workers in California during the Great Depression.
clues.a: What is Of Mice and Men?

clues.q: H. G. Wells's science fiction novel is about an attempted invasion of Earth by beings from Mars.
clues.a: What is The War of the Worlds?

clues.q: This Old English epic poem of 3,182 alliterative lines survives in a single manuscript, the Nowell Codex.
Completed around 1321, this Italian narrative poem by Dante Alighieri presents an imaginative vision of the afterlife.
Virgil's Latin epic poem tells of a Trojan who fled the fall of Troy and travelled to Italy, becoming the ancestor of the Romans.
John Milton's epic poem in blank verse concerns the temptation of Adam and Eve by Satan and their expulsion from the Garden of Eden.
Geoffrey Chaucer's Middle English anthology is framed as a storytelling contest among pilgrims travelling to the shrine of Thomas Becket.
This Dostoevsky novel first appeared in The Russian Messenger in twelve monthly installments during 1866.
Leo Tolstoy called this novel, serialised from 1875 to 1877, his first true novel.
Gabriel Garcia Marquez's 1967 novel tells the multi-generational story of the Buendia family of the fictitious town of Macondo.
clues.a: What is One Hundred Years of Solitude?

clues.q: In this 1915 Franz Kafka novella, salesman Gregor Samsa wakes up to find himself transformed into a huge insect.
Gustave Flaubert's debut novel follows Emma, who lives beyond her means to escape the boredom of provincial life.
Victor Hugo's 1831 Gothic novel set in 15th-century Paris features Quasimodo and the street dancer Esmeralda.
clues.a: What is The Hunchback of Notre-Dame?

clues.q: Samuel Beckett subtitled this play, first written and performed in French, "a tragicomedy in two acts".
This ancient Mesopotamian poem about a king of Uruk is the world's oldest surviving example of narrative literature.
clues.a: What is The Epic of Gilgamesh?

clues.q: This 1890 philosophical and Gothic horror novel is the only novel written by Oscar Wilde.
clues.a: What is The Picture of Dorian Gray?

clues.q: In this 1899 Joseph Conrad novella, the sailor Charles Marlow tells of serving as a steamer captain in the African interior.
Joseph Heller's 1961 debut is a satirical war novel told out of sequence from the points of view of different characters.
John Steinbeck's 1939 Pulitzer-winning novel follows the Joads, tenant farmers driven from their Oklahoma home during the Great Depression.
clues.a: What is The Grapes of Wrath?

clues.q: In this Shakespeare play, Antonio defaults on a large loan from the moneylender Shylock, with seemingly fatal consequences.
clues.a: What is The Merchant of Venice?

clues.q: With over 100 million copies sold, this 1939 Agatha Christie novel is the world's best-selling mystery novel.
clues.a: What is And Then There Were None?

clues.q: This 1826 James Fenimore Cooper novel, the second of the Leatherstocking Tales, is set in 1757 during the French and Indian War.
clues.a: What is The Last of the Mohicans?

clues.q: Frank Herbert's 1965 epic science fiction novel won the first Nebula Award for Best Novel.
Goethe's two-part tragic play, based on a German folk legend, is often called his magnum opus.
Dostoevsky's final novel was serialised in The Russian Messenger from 1879 to 1880; he died less than four months after it was published.
This modernist novel by James Joyce was published in Paris by Sylvia Beach in 1922, on the author's fortieth birthday.
Albert Camus's first published novel follows Meursault, an indifferent man in French Algeria.
In this 1759 Voltaire satire, a sheltered young man is taught optimism by his mentor, Professor Pangloss.
Ovid's Latin narrative poem in 15 books chronicles the world from its creation to the deification of Julius Caesar through over 250 myths.
Written by the lady-in-waiting Murasaki Shikibu in the early 11th century, this Japanese classic is sometimes called the world's first novel.
clues.a: What is The Tale of Genji?

clues.q: This "novel in verse" by Alexander Pushkin, published serially from 1825 to 1832, is a classic of Russian literature.
In this posthumously published Kafka novel, bank official Josef K. is arrested and prosecuted without ever learning his crime.
Marcel Proust's novel in seven volumes is known for its length and its theme of involuntary memory.
clues.a: What is In Search of Lost Time (Remembrance of Things Past)?

clues.q: Goethe wrote this 1774 epistolary novel of the Sturm und Drang period in just five and a half weeks at age 24.
clues.a: What is The Sorrows of Young Werther?

clues.q: This 1842 Nikolai Gogol novel follows the travels of Pavel Ivanovich Chichikov; Gogol called it an "epic poem in prose".
Mikhail Bulgakov wrote this novel in the Soviet Union between 1928 and 1940; a censored version was published after his death.
clues.a: What is The Master and Margarita?

clues.q: Umberto Eco's 1980 debut novel is a historical murder mystery set in an Italian monastery in 1327.
clues.a: What is The Name of the Rose?

clues.q: Refused publication in the USSR, this Boris Pasternak novel about a physician and poet was first published in Italy in 1957.
In this 14th-century Boccaccio work, seven young women and three young men shelter in a villa outside Florence and tell 100 tales.
This 11th-century chanson de geste about the Battle of Roncevaux Pass is the oldest surviving major work of French literature.
clues.a: What is The Song of Roland?

clues.q: This epic poem written around 1200 in Middle High German is based on Germanic heroic legend; its anonymous poet was likely from Passau.
This 16th-century Ming dynasty Chinese novel was known in English through Arthur Waley's 1942 abridged translation titled Monkey.
clues.a: What is Journey to the West?

clues.q: Hermann Hesse's 1922 novel recounts one man's spiritual journey of self-discovery during the time of the Gautama Buddha.

media.q: This John Tenniel illustration of a tea party comes from which 1865 book by Lewis Carroll?
media.a: What is Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?

media.q: W. W. Denslow drew this girl scolding a lion for which 1900 L. Frank Baum book?
media.a: What is The Wonderful Wizard of Oz?

This Ford Madox Brown painting shows the balcony scene from which Shakespeare play?
This 1876 frontispiece by True Williams shows a boy fishing. Which Mark Twain novel is it from?
media.a: What is The Adventures of Tom Sawyer?

media.q: Maurice Leloir drew these four swordsmen for an 1894 edition of which Alexandre Dumas novel?
This illustration shows a boy hiding in an apple barrel aboard the Hispaniola. Which Stevenson novel is it from?
This illustration of a whale attacking a boat is from which 1851 Herman Melville novel?
Gustave Doré drew this old gentleman whose head is crowded with tales of chivalry. Which Cervantes novel is it?
This 1726 first edition claims to be a ship's surgeon's travel memoir. Which Irish satirist really wrote it?
Émile Bayard's drawing of young Cosette comes from which Victor Hugo novel?
Sidney Paget drew this 1902 scene of a man entering a stone hut on a moor. Which Sherlock Holmes novel is it from?
media.a: What is The Hound of the Baskervilles?

media.q: This 1871 frontispiece shows a submarine adventure beneath the waves. Which French author wrote the novel?

media.credit: Édouard Riou and Alphonse de Neuville

media.q: Henry Fuseli painted these three witches from which Shakespeare tragedy set in Scotland?
Hammatt Billings drew this enslaved man and a little girl named Eva for which 1852 Harriet Beecher Stowe novel?
This early-1400s manuscript page shows a pilgrim on horseback from which Geoffrey Chaucer work?
This page of a damaged manuscript begins with 'Hwæt!' Which Old English epic is it?
This 12th-century painted handscroll illustrates which 11th-century Japanese novel by Murasaki Shikibu?
media.a: What is The Tale of Genji?

media.q: Thomas Cole painted this 1827 scene from which James Fenimore Cooper novel?
media.a: What is The Last of the Mohicans?

media.q: This illustration shows Christian with his burden from which 1678 John Bunyan allegory?
